label: PROMPT CV-1: alpha blocker alone
title: Alpha blocker used alone for high blood pressure
statement: The use of alpha-adrenoceptor blocking drugs (e.g. doxazosin, prazosin) as monotherapy for hypertension, should be avoided.

source.document: Cooper JA, et al. The development of the PROMPT criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484, Table 4
source.citation: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484
source.credit: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484

plain_summary: Doxazosin, prazosin or a similar alpha blocker used alone to treat high blood pressure can make blood pressure fall too far when the person stands up.

medicine_groups.name: Alpha-adrenoceptor blockers (alpha blockers)
medicine_groups.note: Tamsulosin, alfuzosin and silodosin are prostate-selective and are not listed.

medicine_groups.name: Other blood pressure medicines (not alpha blockers)
medicine_groups.note: Another blood pressure medicine counts when it is used for hypertension during the alpha-blocker course. Chlorthalidone is another spelling of chlortalidone. Exclude Hemangiol oral liquid. Only oral minoxidil used for hypertension counts. Match the oral hypertension tablets by ingredient or brand and confirm their use. Exclude Dixarit and injectable clonidine or hydralazine. A Catapres line with no form or treatment reason cannot clear the finding by itself. Exclude topical diltiazem or nifedipine and injections. A combination counts only when a qualifying component is being used for hypertension. Entresto alone does not establish this.

rule_for_models: Check a Group A alpha-blocker supply only at ages 45 to 64 inclusive (if age is missing, record eligibility as unknown), and report no finding if the alpha blocker is used only for another reason such as benign prostatic hyperplasia. Suspect a finding and cite the supply and the evidence linking the alpha blocker to hypertension when the alpha blocker treats hypertension, alone or alongside another indication, and no eligible Group B medicine, including a component of a combination, is active for hypertension during that course. When a recorded condition or observation links the medicine to hypertension, cite that line as well. Ignore clearly stopped treatment and report a possible finding that names the missing detail if monotherapy is plausible but the reason for the alpha blocker, or the timing or use of a possible second hypertension treatment, is unclear. A hypertension diagnosis alone does not establish the reason. If the reason is unclear and monotherapy is plausible, name the missing fact "Reason for the alpha blocker".

needs_facts.meets: The record links the alpha blocker under review to treatment of hypertension, either alone or alongside another indication. Hypertension recorded without that link leaves the indication uncertain. Use solely for another condition excludes the finding. If the reason is unknown, keep an otherwise plausible finding possible.

options.words: Urinary symptoms from the prostate only
Both high blood pressure and urinary symptoms from the prostate

cannot_be_seen: Why the alpha blocker was prescribed (blood pressure, prostate symptoms or both), blood pressure readings outside this record, whether other blood pressure medicines were tried and stopped, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the alpha blocker is the best choice for this patient, and what condition it is meant to treat.
